newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Telephone says revs, costs up in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Thai Telephone says revs, costs up in Q1.

text.p: Thai Telephone and Telecommunications Plc said on Friday its operating revenue rose 68 percent while costs and operating expenses jumped 176 percent in the first quarter compared to the same period last year.
The company made the statement to the Stock Exchange of Thailand to explain its first quarter earnings decline to 44.4 million baht ($1.71 million) from 154.7 million the same period last year.

Thai Telephone, one of the country's two private fixed-line phone operators, said operating revenues amounted to 1.45 billon baht in the quarter compared to 861 million baht the first quarter of 1996.
The company said the rise was due to the company's increased number of telephone line installations and subscribers and due to increased use of telephone services.
Costs and operating expenses rose to 685 million baht in the quarter from 148 million baht the same period last year.
Thai Telephone said the jump was partly due to renting a long-distance circuit as well as higher amortisation and depreciation costs of its equipment.
